title: YAGNI Principle
body:
You arent going to need it :)

**"You aren't going to need it."** Build what the current requirement asks for, not what you
guess a future one might. The generalised version, the extra configuration option, the plugin
layer for the second backend nobody has asked for: leave them out.

The argument is not laziness. Speculative work costs three times. You pay to write it, you
pay to carry it (every future reader has to understand code that does nothing yet, which is
[[Complexity]]), and you usually pay to remove it, because the guess was wrong and the real
requirement arrives in a shape the abstraction does not fit. A guessed abstraction is worse
than none: it constrains the design in a direction chosen before anyone knew the answer.

It follows straight out of [[Agile]]. If requirements are expected to change, predictions
about them are worth nothing, so acting on predictions is waste.

The limit: YAGNI is about *features*, not about quality. It is not an argument against
[[Unit testing]], [[Review]], or getting [[Coupling and Cohesion]] right, because those are
what make it cheap to add the thing later when it turns out you did need it. Skipping those
is how you end up unable to change anything, which is the failure YAGNI is trying to avoid.

Related: [[software development]], [[Design]], [[Code Smells]].
